run.answer: Everything is gathered and the tabs are in their final state. Here's your build note. --- ## Build note — React art prototype assets ### 1. Recommended IDE (JetBrains) **WebStorm** — JetBrains positions it explicitly as *"The JavaScript and TypeScript IDE"* (homepage lists it as "IDE for JavaScript"; product page tagline: "The JavaScript and TypeScript IDE"). It's ready out of the box for JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, **React**, Angular, Vue and Node.js, with built-in refactoring, navigation, debugging, Git, and package-manager tooling — i.e., exactly "editing and organizing web code." It's free for non-commercial use, which fits a prototype. *(Tab open: jetbrains.com/webstorm/)* ### 2. Mouse image (transparent) + Stretchy comparison - **Source page (open):** Wikimedia Commons — *File:Mouse clipart.svg*, a cartoon mouse clipart, **CC0 public domain** (no attribution required, free for commercial use): `https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mouse_clipart.svg` - **Direct image (open):** transparent PNG render at 1280px: `https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Mouse_clipart.svg/1280px-Mouse_clipart.svg.png` - **Transparency check:** this is a vector SVG with *no background rectangle*, so the PNG render is genuinely alpha-transparent — on the direct-image tab you should see your browser's page (or a checkerboard in a dev tool) showing through, not white. (The raw SVG is also open in a tab: `https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5b/Mouse_clipart.svg`.) - **Stretchy (open):** Taffy Tails wiki page — `https://taffy-tails.fandom.com/wiki/Stretchy`. Per the wiki, Stretchy is "one of the main four candy monsters of Taffy Tails… an animated Taffy," with a gallery of character renders for your style comparison. - *Caveat:* Google Images itself blocked me with a captcha, so the image search ran via Bing. I also found a rawpixel-hosted "Png cartoon mouse clipart, transparent" (1000×1250) in Bing's results, but its host timed out twice when I tried to open it directly, so I couldn't verify it — the Commons CC0 mouse above is the verified, usable one. ### 3. React component (react-svgr.com) The SVGR Playground is open at `https://react-svgr.com/playground/` with a basic SVG already converted and the result visible in the JSX OUTPUT pane: ```jsx import * as React from "react" const SvgComponent = (props) => ( ) export default SvgComponent ``` To get the *mouse* as a component: paste the contents of the open SVG tab into the **SVG INPUT** box (the editor is a code widget I couldn't type into programmatically) and the JSX updates live. For a quick prototype you can also inline the mouse as a background-image ``/CSS to pair the vector element with the raster. ### 4. CapCut — Web → Desktop - **Official guidance (open: capcut.com help "Can I link my CapCut Mobile and PC Accounts?"):** linking accounts syncs "account information and projects across devices." Recommended flow: log in on mobile first → launch CapCut desktop → Sign in via **QR code** → scan from the mobile app → projects, drafts and account data sync automatically (internet required). - **Current third-party guide (capcutguide.com, checked Sep 2026 against CapCut Help):** the supported cross-device route is uploading the **editable project to a Space (project sync)** and opening it on the destination device; a raw draft-folder copy is *not* a guaranteed importable package; note that "deleting a Web project affects linked devices." Verify the destination timeline, media, fonts and an export before retiring the original. Community reports (Reddit) show web-started projects appearing in the desktop app with an "uploaded from CapCut web" note, so expect some web-only features to be missing on desktop. ### 5. CapCut — background color behind an imported photo Per the official guide (open: capcut.com/resource/change-image-background-color): 1. Open CapCut and **import your image** (the mouse PNG). 2. **Auto background removal** first (removes the backdrop so only the mouse remains). 3. In the **Background** menu, select **"Background color"** and pick from the color palette. 4. Apply (one-click) and fine-tune the hue as needed. **Tailored to your assets:** since the Commons mouse PNG is truly transparent, you can skip the removal step — just drop it on the timeline and set the Background color to match your page. If the **generic cartoon mouse** wins, a soft cream/grey background suits its flat clipart look; if you lean **Stretchy-style** (candy/taffy character), a saturated candy color (pink/teal) will match that style better. For the promo clip, keep the mouse on an upper track over the color background track so you can re-color without touching the asset. ### Tabs left open for you | Tab | What | |---|---| | 3 | WebStorm (JetBrains web IDE) | | 5 | Stretchy — Taffy Tails wiki | | 6 | react-svgr playground (component visible) | | 10 | CapCut account linking / project sync (official) | | 12 | CapCut change image background color (official) | | 13 | Mouse clipart source page (Wikimedia Commons, CC0) | | 14 | Direct transparent PNG of the mouse | | 15 | Raw mouse SVG (paste into SVGR) |
